title: Enterprise Stabilization: Technical Sweep & SLA Readiness Checklist
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a coordinated technical sweep and SLA readiness checklist for enterprise go-lives during the first 14 days after cutover. It is designed for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Platform SRE, Product Ops, and the customer's technical leads to validate production readiness, confirm SLO alignment, and establish a backstop for fast mitigation of any regression in availability, latency, or cost.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success (primary)
- Eng SRE and Platform teams
- Onboarding Solutions Engineers
- Customer technical contacts and architecture owners

Goals:
- Verify telemetry, alerting, and dashboards are accurately reflecting tenant traffic within 48 hours of cutover.
- Confirm SLA eligibility and billing flags are correct prior to first billing cycle.
- Execute lightweight smoke and regression checks for core flows (generation, embeddings, streaming) at production scale for the customer traffic profile.
- Establish a documented mitigation and rollback path if SLOs are breached.

When to run this playbook:
1) Immediately after tenant cutover in staging -> production (day 0) for an initial smoke sweep.
2) Full technical sweep during day 1–3 to validate telemetry, throttles, and model fallbacks.
3) SLA readiness confirmation and billing gating on day 7 and day 14.

Ownership and contacts:
- CSE Onboarding Lead: Asha Patel (owner)
- Platform SRE Incident Lead: Marcus Nguyen
- Product Ops (billing gate): Lena Ortiz
- Escalation path: eng-sre-oncall -> platform-incident -> customer-success-manager

High-level coordination checklist (roles):
- CSE: coordinate customer runbook, run smoke tests, validate sample prompts, confirm token accounting.
- SRE: confirm alert routing, synthetic checks, latency percentiles, and circuit-breakers.
- Product Ops: verify usage metering, free-credit accounting, and SLA flags.
- Customer: provide production traffic pattern, hold a 30-minute daily sync for first 72 hours.

Pre-sweep prerequisites (verify these before starting):
- Deployment flag for tenant set to PRODUCTION and correct model pins applied.
- Ingress certificates valid and client certs authenticated (if mutual TLS used).
- Observability forwarding configured for tenant (metrics, traces, logs).
- Billing tenant_id set and test charge accepted in sandbox.
- SLO definitions imported into the tenant record (latency P50/P95, availability).

Technical sweep procedure (Step-by-step):
1) Smoke tests (immediate, ~30–60 minutes):
   a) Validate health endpoints: curl -sS https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health | jq .
   b) Run 10 production-like generation requests using customer's sample prompts. Capture latency and tokens used.
   c) Confirm streaming connection setup (websocket/wss) and EOF behavior with 5 streaming requests.

2) Telemetry and sampling validation (within 4 hours):
   a) Confirm traces appear in X-Ray/Jaeger for these requests with span names: request.receive, runtime.batch, kv.cache.hit, runtime.render.
   b) Check metrics in Grafana: tenant.<tenant_id>.requests_total, token_count, latency_ms.p50, latency_ms.p95, error_rate. Expected baselines should be within +/-20% of staging profile.

3) Rate limit and quota exercise (within 8 hours):
   a) Simulate burst at 1.5x expected peak to validate adaptive rate-limiter behavior.
   b) Validate 429 handling and graceful backoff behavior in client.

4) Model fallback and compatibility (24 hours):
   a) Trigger a model variant cutoff (simulate an out-of-capacity fallback) and confirm auto-fallback to pinned-compatible-model returns correct format and acceptable quality.

5) Cost and meter sanity (day 1–3):
   a) Inspect token accounting for test requests vs. expected cost models.
   b) Verify the usage connector has forwarded billing rows to Billing pipeline with tenant tag.

6) SLO and alert confirmation (day 1):
   a) Confirm alerting rules fire on synthetics when latency or error budget thresholds are crossed.
   b) Validate escalation flow triggers pager when a high-severity alert threshold is breached.

SLA readiness gating table (to be signed by Product Ops and CSE):
| Gate | Criterion | Pass Signal | Owner | Deadline |
|-----|----------|------------|-------|---------|
| Telemetry | Metrics and traces visible for tenant | Grafana and Jaeger traces with tenant tag | SRE | Day 1 EOD |
| Functionality | Core API requests succeed at expected success rate (>99%) | Synthetic pass rate >= 99% for 1hr | CSE | Day 1 |
| Latency | P95 latency within SLO target (configurable by customer) | P95 < configured threshold for 30m window | SRE | Day 3 |
| Billing | Usage rows present and mapped to tenant with expected token accounting | Billing pipeline shows non-zero rows for test traffic | Product Ops | Day 7 |
| SLA Flag | Tenant eligible flag set for SLA and billing protections | Manual approval in Billing console | Product Ops | Day 14 |

NOTE: If any gate fails, follow the Mitigation and Rollback section below before approving SLA flag.

Common validation commands and snippets:
- Check recent metrics: kubectl exec -it grafana-query -- curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(tenant_requests_total[5m])" | jq .
- Sample generation request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-v1","input":"Summarize customer invoice records for April.","max_tokens":200}' | jq .
- Streaming test (node example):
  const ws = new WebSocket('wss://stream.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?tenant=$TENANT');
  ws.on('open', () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-xl-v1',input:'Hello'})));

Telemetry assertions (quick checklist):
- Tenant tag present on request metrics and billing metrics.
- KV cache hit ratio reported in telemetry (should be between 10%–60% depending on workload).
- CPU/GPU utilization per node under 85% for sustained 5-minute window.
- Error rate per route < 1% (excluding expected 429s during rate-limit tests).

Mitigation and rollback options (ordered by preference):
1) Feature-level rollback: disable new feature flags (CSE/Product) and continue traffic on previous path.
2) Model variant switch: pin customer to previous model version with known stable profile.
3) Traffic diversion: redirect subset of tenant traffic to a safe capacity pool (dedicated to burst/fallback).
4) Tenant freeze: throttle requests to a safe limit while extended investigation completes.
5) Emergency rollback: revert cutover and return to the old endpoint (requires coordinated release and database state verification).

Escalation playbook (if SLO breached):
1) Declare SEV-1 if availability < 99% for > 15 minutes or latency > 2x SLO for > 30 minutes.
2) Notify oncall SRE, CSE owner, Product Ops, and customer primary via designated Slack channel and incident bridge.
3) Run triage checklist: gather logs, top 10 error stacks, recent deploys, quota and KVM cache metrics.
4) If mitigation above cannot restore service within 30 minutes, initiate traffic diversion.

Communication plan with customer:
- Day 0: immediate post-cutover email with links to dashboards, daily sync times, and escalation contacts.
- Day 1–3: 30-minute daily sync (standup) to review telemetry and runbook actions.
- Day 7: SLA readiness summary and ask for sign-off on billing gate.
- Day 14: Final stabilization review and transition to standard support cadence.

Acceptance signoff template (copy into meeting notes):
- CSE confirms telemetry and functionality gates: YES/NO
- SRE confirms alerting and latency gates: YES/NO
- Product Ops confirms billing and SLA flag: YES/NO
- Customer confirms acceptance and operational readiness: YES/NO

Appendices:
A) Quick reference: typical SLO defaults
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for enterprise Dedicated tenants (changeable by contract)
- Latency: P50 50ms, P95 300ms (depends on model and region)
- Error budget: 0.1% monthly

B) Example synthetic test payloads
- Short generation: {"model":"redwood-small","input":"Give three bullet points about product packaging."}
- Embedding batch sample (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-compact-v1","inputs":["invoice text 1","invoice text 2"]}' | jq .

C) Ops contacts and escalation channels
- Slack: #oncall-sre, #cse-enterprise, #platform-ops
- Pager: +1-555-0100 (primary oncall)
- Incident bridge: https://meet.example.com/incident-bridge
